sections.title: The ending tion
paragraphs: The ending tion is spoken as /ʃən/. It sounds like the end of the word (action) /æk.ʃən/, which means an act or movement. This ending makes two different sounds in English words.

sections.title: How to say tion
paragraphs: For the first sound, round your lips slightly. Push air through the gap without your voice, then relax into a weak ending. For the second sound, press the tip of your tongue behind your top front teeth. Release the air suddenly with a soft hiss before the weak ending. Hold your hand against your throat to feel that your voice stays off during both starts.

sections.title: Spelling rules for tion
paragraphs: In most words, this ending is unstressed and makes the sound /ʃən/, as heard in (nation) /neɪ.ʃən/. When the letters come right after the letter s, they make the sound /tʃən/, as heard in (question) /kwes.tʃən/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with tion
paragraphs: Do not read the letters as separate sounds like tee on. Always use a soft rushing sound or a quick stop sound at the start. Do not say a clear vowel like on at the end. Keep the final vowel very short and weak, so it does not sound like the full vowel in off.
